analytical_dimensions.description: What the reader says the work argues
probing_questions: For each statement, what does the reader say the named work argues, on what clue, and which part of the memo does it bear on?

analytical_dimensions.description: What the work says on that matter
probing_questions: What does the held text argue on the matter the reader raises, where, and in whose voice?

analytical_dimensions.description: Whether the recollection holds, and what it implies
probing_questions: Does the recollection hold, hold in part, diverge, fall outside the text or stay unverifiable; and what does that imply for the part it bears on?

analytical_dimensions.description: What the desk should ask next
probing_questions: Which questions do the divergences and the texts license, and which would change the part most?

engine_name: Your references, re-read against the texts
problematique: A reader commented on a memo and named works from memory ("Sewell's critique of Brenner on the Dutch case"). The comment is the document under test, as numbered statements each citing the works it names; the works are held in full. For each statement say what the reader says the work argues, what the work says on that matter in its own words, whether the recollection holds, holds in part, diverges, is not in the text or cannot be checked, and what that implies for the part of the memo the statement bears on. Then the follow-up questions the sources license, at most three, each anchored in a text, ranked by how much an answer would change the part. Never supply what a work says from memory; an unheld work stays unverifiable. Precise about voice, edition and scope.
researcher_question: Do the reader's recollections of the works they named hold against those works, and what should the desk ask them next?
